question: According to BS 7671, what is the maximum earth fault loop impedance (Zs) permitted for a 32A Type B circuit breaker to BS EN 60898 to ensure disconnection within 0.4 seconds in a TN system?

A three-phase 400V motor has a full-load current of 45A. Using IEE guidance, what minimum cable cross-sectional area (copper, PVC insulated, clipped direct) is required if the cable has a grouping factor of 0.70 and an ambient temperature correction factor of 0.87?
options: 16 mm²
25 mm²
35 mm²
10 mm²

question: In a TT earthing system, RCD protection is mandatory for virtually all circuits because:
options: The prospective fault current is too high for overcurrent devices to operate safely
The earth fault loop impedance is typically too high for overcurrent protective devices to disconnect within required times
The neutral conductor impedance causes excessive voltage drop
The supply transformer impedance prevents correct fuse operation

question: Which of the following correctly describes the purpose of an equipotential bonding conductor installed to a gas installation pipe at the meter position?
options: To carry fault current back to the transformer star point
To reduce touch voltage to a safe level by raising the potential of exposed metalwork to that of the installation earth
To provide a return path for leakage current from the gas pipe
To supplement the main earthing terminal in the event of a neutral failure

question: When applying the adiabatic equation S = √(I²t) / k to verify a protective conductor size, what does the factor 'k' represent?
options: The fault current in amperes
A factor accounting for the resistivity, temperature coefficient and heat capacity of the conductor material
The disconnection time of the protective device in seconds
The cross-sectional area of the conductor in mm²

question: A single-phase 230V circuit has a design current (Ib) of 28A. A 32A BS EN 60898 Type C MCB is selected. The cable is installed in thermal insulation for 0.6 m. What condition must be satisfied for the cable rating after applying the correction factor for insulation (0.5) and any other derating?
options: It ≥ In only
It ≥ Ib and It ≥ In / (product of all correction factors)
It ≥ In × 1.45
It ≥ Ib × 1.25 only

question: Under BS 7671 Regulation 421.1.201, a consumer unit installed in a domestic premises must have its enclosure manufactured from:
options: Steel or other ferrous metal
Non-combustible material or be enclosed in a cabinet of non-combustible material
Any material rated to 650°C
Polycarbonate with a fire-retardant additive only

question: What is the principal function of a surge protective device (SPD) Type 1 installed at the origin of an installation?
options: To protect against conducted overvoltages from switching operations within the installation
To divert direct lightning strike currents and limit the resulting overvoltage to safe levels
To filter high-frequency harmonics generated by non-linear loads
To provide overcurrent protection for sensitive electronic equipment

question: In a 3-phase 4-wire system supplying a mix of single-phase non-linear loads, the neutral conductor may carry current exceeding the line current because:
options: The power factor correction capacitors inject reactive current into the neutral
Triplen harmonics (3rd, 9th, 15th…) produced by non-linear loads are in-phase and add arithmetically in the neutral
The neutral has higher impedance, causing voltage unbalance and increased current flow
Negative sequence currents cancel in the line conductors and sum in the neutral

question: A ring final circuit is tested for continuity using the end-to-end method. The line conductor resistance measured end-to-end is 0.8 Ω and the CPC resistance is 1.2 Ω. What is the expected maximum r1 + r2 value at the furthest socket outlet?
Which instrument characteristic is most critical when measuring insulation resistance on a circuit that includes electronic equipment connected in parallel?
options: The test voltage must be 1000V DC to ensure accurate results
A low test voltage (250V DC) should be selected to avoid damaging semiconductor components
The instrument must have an accuracy class of 0.5 or better
The test leads must have a resistance below 0.1 Ω

question: When calculating voltage drop for a 3-phase balanced circuit using BS 7671 tables, the formula used is:
options: VD = (mV/A/m × Ib × L) / 1000
VD = (mV/A/m × Ib × L) / 1000 where mV/A/m is taken from the appropriate table for the conductor size and installation method
VD = I² × R × L
VD = V × I × cos φ × L

question: What does a phase rotation test confirm on a newly installed three-phase motor circuit before energisation?
options: That the insulation resistance exceeds 1 MΩ between phases
That the sequence of phases (L1, L2, L3) matches the motor's designed rotation direction to prevent mechanical damage
That the protective conductor continuity is satisfactory
That the earth fault loop impedance is within permitted limits

question: Under the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989, Regulation 4(3) states that work on or near live conductors is only permissible if:
options: The system voltage is below 230V and a second person is present
It is unreasonable to work dead, adequate precautions are taken, and it is reasonable to work live
A permit-to-work has been issued by the local Distribution Network Operator
The worker holds a minimum Level 3 qualification in electrical installation

question: A prospective short-circuit current (PSCC) measurement at a distribution board is recorded as 6 kA. The installed MCBs are rated at 6 kA breaking capacity. Which action is required?
options: No action required as the breaking capacity exactly matches the PSCC
Replace the MCBs with devices having a breaking capacity exceeding 6 kA, or verify that upstream device let-through energy provides adequate back-up protection
Increase the cross-sectional area of all outgoing cables by one size
Install additional RCDs on each outgoing circuit to limit fault current
